channel.title: Tesla recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Front Suspension Connections May Loosen
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because hardware securing one or more front suspension links may not have been tightened properly. A link could loosen or come away from the vehicle's supporting frame. Tesla Service will tighten or replace the securing hardware, check wheel alignment, and replace related parts that have been damaged if needed. The work is free.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y Headlights Too Bright
item.description: On certain Tesla Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, the low beam headlights may shine brighter than they are allowed to be. Headlights that are too bright can reduce how well oncoming drivers are able to see the road, other vehicles, and their surroundings. This reduced visibility for drivers coming the other way raises the chance of a crash happening.

item.title: Model 3 Vehicles Missing Required Safety Features
item.description: Certain Tesla vehicles were originally built for a foreign market and do not have knee air bags. They may also be missing certain interior safety features and may not have been tested for bumper impact resistance. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for occupant crash protection, interior impact protection, and bumper standards.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Missing Vehicle Certification Label
item.description: Some affected vehicles may not have had the certification label installed. This label provides weight information for the vehicle. Without it, an owner could unintentionally overload the vehicle.

item.title: Tesla Model 3, S and Y rearview camera image delayed
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model 3, Model S, Model X and Model Y vehicles that are running software version 2026.8.6. When the vehicle is put into reverse, the picture from the rearview camera may be delayed before it appears. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Tesla has released a software update that reaches the vehicle over the air, at no cost.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Wheel Stud May Separate
item.description: Certain Cybertrucks with 18-inch steel wheels have brake rotors whose stud holes may crack. If that happens, a wheel stud can separate from the wheel hub.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Off-Road Light Bar May Detach
item.description: Some Cybertrucks with a service-installed off-road light bar accessory may have been assembled using the wrong surface primer to attach the light bar to the windshield. Because the wrong primer was used, the light bar can loosen and come loose from the windshield.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Front Parking Lights Too Bright
item.description: Certain 2024 to 2026 Cybertruck vehicles running software older than a specific version may have front parking lights that shine brighter than what safety rules allow. When these lights are too bright, they can make it harder for other drivers on the road to see clearly, which raises the chance of a crash. This happens because of how the vehicle's software controls the parking lights on these trucks.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Battery Contacts May Fail
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because electrical contacts in the battery pack may fail. This failure can cause the vehicle to lose drive power. The recall also includes certain Model 3 vehicles. Tesla Service will replace the affected electrical contacts in the battery pack free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Reverse Lights May Not Illuminate
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because a wiring defect may prevent the reverse lights from turning on when the vehicle is in reverse. The vehicles do not meet the federal safety requirement listed in the notice for vehicle lights and related equipment. Tesla Service will replace the reverse lights and their wiring assembly free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Horn May Stop Working
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because a connection on the horn's ground wire may not be secured properly. The electrical connection could break, preventing the horn from sounding. Tesla service will replace the steering wheel to address the recall, and the replacement is free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y Seat Fasteners May Be Loose
item.description: Certain Tesla Model 3 and Model Y vehicles may have improperly tightened fasteners connecting the seat back to the seat bottom. The affected seat may not hold its occupant properly during a crash. Tesla Service Centers will inspect these fasteners and tighten or replace them as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Washer Spray May Be Blocked
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because a hose connector may block the windshield washer spray openings. This can prevent washer fluid from reaching the windshield, leaving the driver unable to clean it. The vehicles do not meet federal windshield wiping and washing requirements. Tesla service will inspect the affected connector and replace it if necessary.

item.title: Tesla Model S Airbag Defect May Silence Horn
item.description: Some Tesla Model S and Model X vehicles were built with an airbag that has the wrong horn pad installed. Because of this mismatched part, pressing the horn does not make it sound. This means the horn does not work as intended, so a driver is not able to use it to alert other drivers on the road the way the horn is supposed to work.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Light Bar Can Detach
item.description: On certain Cybertrucks, the light bar can come loose and separate from the vehicle. Once detached, it can end up in the road as a hazard for other drivers.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 Power Steering Assist May Fail
item.description: Some Tesla Model 3 vehicles running older software can experience a problem with the power steering system. A circuit board for the electric power steering assist can become overstressed and cause the power steering assist to stop working right when the car comes to a stop and then starts moving again. When that happens, the steering wheel becomes much harder to turn, especially at low speeds.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y May Lose Backup Camera
item.description: In certain Tesla vehicles, a circuit board inside the car's computer can short out and the picture from the rearview camera can be lost. Without that image, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Tesla has sent out a free software update over the air. Tesla will also find vehicles whose computer board has failed or is under strain that could lead to failure, and replace those computers free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model S driver airbag may tear during deployment
item.description: The driver's airbag could tear as it deploys. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for occupant crash protection and windshield mounting.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck, Model 3, Model Y tire pressure warning light fault
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Cybertruck, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. The warning light for the tire pressure monitoring system may not stay lit from one drive to the next. When that happens, the system does not warn the driver that a tire is low on air. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal rules for tire pressure monitoring systems. Tesla has already released a software update that fixes it.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Drive Inverter Fault Cuts Power
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain 2024 Cybertruck vehicles because a fault in the drive inverter may cause a loss of drive power to the wheels, meaning the vehicle may stop being able to move under its own power. Tesla service will replace the drive inverter to fix the problem. Owner notification letters about this recall have already been mailed to affected owners, and the repair will be done free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Rearview Camera Image May Be Delayed
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain 2024 Cybertruck vehicles because the rearview camera image may be delayed after the driver shifts into reverse. A delayed image gives the driver less view of what's behind the vehicle when backing up, which the notice says increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Tesla Hood Latch May Not Detect Unlatched Hood
item.description: Some Tesla Model 3, Model S, Model X, and Model Y vehicles have a hood latch that may fail to detect when the hood isn't fully latched. If the hood isn't properly closed, it could open fully while driving, blocking the driver's view of the road. Tesla is fixing this with a free over-the-air software update, so no dealer visit is needed.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Trim Applique May Come Loose
item.description: Some Tesla Cybertruck vehicles have a trim piece on the trunk bed, called the sail applique, that may not have been glued on properly during assembly. Because the adhesive was not applied the right way, this trim piece can gradually loosen over time. If it loosens enough, the piece can detach and come off the vehicle completely, since it is only held on with adhesive.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Windshield Wiper Motor May Fail
item.description: Too much electrical current can build up in the front windshield wiper system and cause the wiper motor controller to stop working. When the wiper motor controller fails, the windshield wipers may stop working. Without working wipers, it can be harder for the driver to see the road clearly, which increases the risk of a crash. To fix this, Tesla will replace the wiper motor free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Seat Belt Warning Chime May Not Activate
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model S, Model X, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. If the driver is not wearing a seat belt, the seat belt warning light and audible chime may not turn on the way they are supposed to. This means the vehicle may fail to alert an unbelted driver that their seat belt is not fastened.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 Side Airbag Missing Deflector Part
item.description: The driver seat side airbag on the affected vehicle was built without a deflector part that directs the airbag's gas flow when it deploys. Without this part, the airbag may not deploy the way it's designed to.

item.title: Tesla Cybertruck Accelerator Pedal Can Get Trapped
item.description: The pad on the accelerator pedal may come loose and get caught by the interior trim. If that happens, the pedal can become trapped, which can cause the vehicle to accelerate without the driver intending it.

item.title: Tesla pedestrian warning sound muted after a factory reset
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model S, Model X, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. Doing a factory reset on the car turned off the sound the car makes so that people walking nearby can hear it coming. With that sound muted, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule on minimum sound for electric and hybrid vehicles. Tesla has put out a software update that the car receives over the air.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Cybertruck warning lights too small
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck vehicles. The Brake, Park and Antilock Braking System warning lights on the instrument panel are shown in the wrong font size, smaller than it should be. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standards for hydraulic, electric and light vehicle brake systems. Tesla has begun sending out a free over-the-air software update to fix the display.

item.title: Tesla Autosteer controls may allow driver misuse
item.description: Tesla is recalling Model S, Model X, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles that have Autosteer, a driver-assistance feature that helps steer the car. Autosteer still requires the driver to stay in charge of driving and take over when needed. In certain situations, the way the feature's controls are presented may not be clear or noticeable enough to keep drivers from using Autosteer in ways it was not designed for, or to make clear when it is not on.

item.title: Tesla Model S/X May Have Wrong Airbag Installed
item.description: Some Tesla Model S and Model X vehicles may have an incorrect airbag installed. This can happen if the steering yoke or round steering wheel was replaced with a different style of yoke or wheel. The airbag that was installed may not be designed to work correctly with that replacement part. Tesla Service will inspect the vehicle and replace the driver airbag as necessary.

item.title: Tesla Model S and Model X Seat Belt Defect
item.description: On some 2021-2023 Tesla Model S and Model X vehicles, the front-row seat belts may not be properly connected to their pretensioner anchors, which can cause a seat belt to detach.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 Battery Disconnect May Fail
item.description: A part designed to disconnect the vehicle's high-voltage battery may be defective. If this part fails, the battery may not be properly isolated after a crash or after the vehicle's system detects a fault. This can increase the risk of electrical shock and injury to people near or in the vehicle. To address this, Tesla will replace the battery disconnect part free of charge.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 Front Suspension Fasteners May Loosen
item.description: On certain Tesla Model 3 vehicles, the fasteners that hold the front suspension's lateral link to the sub-frame may loosen over time. If they loosen enough, the lateral link can separate from the sub-frame entirely, changing how the vehicle's wheel is aligned.

item.title: Tesla Full Self-Driving Beta may act unsafely at intersections
item.description: Tesla is recalling Model S, Model X, Model 3 and Model Y vehicles that have the Full Self-Driving Beta software, or are waiting for it to be installed. The software may let the car behave unsafely at intersections, for example going straight through an intersection from a turn-only lane, entering a stop-sign intersection without coming to a full stop, or going into an intersection on a steady yellow light. It may also respond poorly to changes in posted speed limits or allow speeding.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y Taillight Failure
item.description: One or both taillights on certain vehicles may sometimes fail to light up. This is an intermittent problem, meaning the taillight might work at times and stop working at other times. When a taillight isn't lit, the vehicle becomes harder for other drivers to see, which reduces its visibility on the road.

item.title: Tesla Model S Side Mirrors Missing Warning Etching
item.description: The outside rearview mirrors on your Model S don't meet federal visibility standards. The mirror on the driver's side is curved, or convex, glass instead of flat glass. The mirror on the passenger's side is missing the etched warning that reads 'Objects in Mirror Are Closer Than They Appear.' Because these mirrors are the wrong type, the vehicle doesn't meet the federal rear visibility safety standard.

item.title: Tesla Model S and X Can Lose Power Steering
item.description: The electric power steering system in your Model S or Model X may lose its power assist while you're driving on rough roads or after hitting a pothole. When that happens, it can be harder to turn the wheel, especially at low speeds. Tesla has released a free over-the-air software update that recalibrates the power steering system to fix this.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 rear seat belts may be reassembled incorrectly
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model 3 vehicles. On these cars, the buckle for the left seat belt in the second row and the anchor for the middle seat belt in the second row may have been put back together incorrectly during a service visit. Tesla Service will inspect the seat belt anchors and put them back together properly where that is needed. The work is done at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Tesla power windows may not stop for an obstruction
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model 3, Model S, Model X and Model Y vehicles because of the power windows. When a window is closing and something is in the way, the system that is supposed to sense it and stop the window may not respond the way it should. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule for power-operated window systems.
